title: Poetic Pebbles overview
content: Poetic Pebbles is an Android community for readers and writers of poetry. It gives writers a focused place to submit poems and gives readers a way to discover approved poems, like work, comment and follow authors. The app is available on Google Play.

title: Poetic Pebbles ownership and timeline
content: Aman Kaushik is the solo developer of Poetic Pebbles. Development started in March 2025, and the Android app was published on Google Play in April 2025. The project is actively maintained.

title: Poetic Pebbles Android architecture
content: Poetic Pebbles uses a Firebase-backed Android architecture designed for secure access, moderated publishing and real-time community interaction. The Android application was developed using Kotlin and XML. Firebase supports authentication, real-time data synchronization, media storage and user notifications.

title: Poetic Pebbles poem approval workflow
content: After a signed-in author creates a poem, its information is stored in Firebase Realtime Database with a pending review status. The poem is not public immediately. The administrative application reviews it and approves or rejects it. Approved poems then become visible in the public feed, where readers can like, comment and follow authors.

title: Poetic Pebbles administrative application
content: The separate Poetic Pebbles administrative application provides centralized tools to review and approve or reject poems, ban or unban users, send broadcast notifications and create Instagram-ready posts. It supports content quality, community safety, communication and social-media content creation.

title: Poetic Pebbles Firebase services
content: Poetic Pebbles uses Firebase Authentication for sign-in and personalized access, Firebase Realtime Database for application data and publishing and engagement workflows, Firebase Storage for user profile pictures, and Firebase Cloud Messaging for like, follow and administrative broadcast notifications.

title: Poetic Pebbles development challenges
content: Key Poetic Pebbles challenges included implementing useful, correctly targeted real-time notifications for likes, new followers and administrative broadcasts; preventing duplicate likes and follow relationships with validation and state checks; keeping Firebase database, storage, network and notification usage practical and cost-conscious; and preparing, testing and publishing the signed Android build on Google Play.

title: Poetic Pebbles lessons learned
content: Building Poetic Pebbles reinforced that a product requires connected authentication, publishing, moderation, engagement, notifications, administration and release management. It also highlighted the importance of modelling data relationships around behaviour, treating moderation and useful notifications as core product features, planning for Firebase cost during design, learning from user feedback and continuously evolving a published product.

title: Poetic Pebbles community impact
content: Since its April 2025 Google Play release, Poetic Pebbles has reached more than 150 users/downloads and contains more than 100 poems. It remains actively maintained, with improvements and new functionality influenced by user suggestions.

title: Poetic Pebbles Instagram community
content: Aman also created an Instagram presence for Poetic Pebbles, where selected poems submitted by users are published and promoted. This extends the community beyond the Android app and helps its writing reach a broader audience.

title: Poetic Pebbles AI roadmap
content: Poetic Pebbles AI is in development and is not currently live in the production Android application. It is planned as a RAG-based assistant that will let users ask natural-language questions about the app, its features, poems and authors.

title: HireSense AI overview
content: HireSense AI is a local, privacy-oriented recruitment-support prototype independently designed and developed by Aman Kaushik. It combines machine learning, NLP, retrieval-augmented generation and a local LLM to help recruiters screen resumes, explore candidate information, compare resumes with job requirements and prepare focused interviews. It is advisory and does not make final hiring decisions.

title: HireSense AI timeline and status
content: Aman started HireSense AI in April 2026. It currently runs locally through a Streamlit interface and Ollama, is actively improving, and deployment is being prepared. It is not currently presented as a deployed or production-ready application.

title: HireSense AI resume input modes
content: HireSense AI supports three input modes: the included CSV candidate dataset, uploaded text-based PDF resumes, and manually entered or pasted resume text. The PDF flow supports text-based PDFs; it is not presented as OCR support for scanned resumes.

title: HireSense AI resume preprocessing
content: A shared preprocessing pipeline cleans and normalizes resume text, removes duplicate records, handles missing values, calculates resume length, derives experience level, and extracts candidate name, skills, education and experience. It creates a consistent representation for different input modes.

title: HireSense AI ML classification
content: HireSense AI uses a Random Forest Classifier as its primary shortlist classifier, with Logistic Regression as a baseline. On the 64-candidate held-out test set (32 shortlisted and 32 not shortlisted), Random Forest achieved 96.88% accuracy, 100.00% precision, 93.75% recall and 96.77% F1. It made 62 correct predictions, with 30 true positives, 32 true negatives, 0 false positives and 2 false negatives. Five-fold cross-validation F1 was 99.68%. Logistic Regression achieved 95.31% accuracy, 100.00% precision, 90.62% recall and 95.08% F1. These are prototype metrics from a small balanced dataset, not production hiring accuracy.

title: HireSense AI match-score model status
content: The match-score regression pipeline is functional, but re-evaluation is required. Its latest feature list still includes shortlist status as an input when predicting match score. Because shortlist status is strongly related to match score, current regression results may be inflated. The feature must be removed, both regressors retrained, and new R², MAE and RMSE values generated before regression performance is presented as verified. Target-leakage correction is required; it is not fixed.

title: HireSense AI NLP and TF-IDF analysis
content: HireSense AI applies TF-IDF keyword analysis and skill-frequency analysis to candidate resumes. Candidate information is represented in a knowledge base and vectorized with TF-IDF for retrieval-oriented search.

title: HireSense AI top-five RAG retrieval
content: For a natural-language recruiter query, HireSense AI uses TF-IDF vectorization and cosine similarity to retrieve the five most relevant candidate resumes. This lightweight RAG workflow helps recruiters search candidate information conversationally instead of manually filtering spreadsheet columns.

title: HireSense AI local Llama 3.2 workflow
content: HireSense AI runs Llama 3.2 locally through Ollama. Local LLM assistance supports professional resume summaries, job-description generation, resume-to-job match analysis, targeted interview questions and an advisory final recommendation. Local execution keeps resume content on the local machine during LLM processing, while speed depends on hardware and Ollama availability.

title: HireSense AI Streamlit dashboard
content: The Python Streamlit application exposes a dashboard, resume screening, RAG search, candidate insights and model-evaluation views. It is currently a local application and deployment preparation is in progress.

title: HireSense AI interview-question threshold
content: HireSense AI generates interview questions only when the resume-to-job match score is above 75%. The questions and final recommendation are advisory and require recruiter review.

title: HireSense AI development challenges
content: Key challenges include normalizing CSV, text-based PDF and manual resume inputs; extracting information from varied resumes without claiming OCR; connecting structured ML, unstructured LLM analysis and RAG; validating structured LLM JSON output; handling local Ollama availability and delays; preventing misleading regression leakage; working with a small balanced dataset; and protecting sensitive resume information.

title: HireSense AI lessons learned
content: HireSense AI reinforced that leakage checks and decision-time feature availability matter before reporting performance; metrics need dataset context; TF-IDF RAG can improve access to structured data; local LLMs trade privacy benefits for operational handling; shared preprocessing supports consistency; generated output needs validation; human oversight is essential; and production readiness requires testing, privacy controls, monitoring and reliable failure handling.

title: HireSense AI responsible-AI limitations
content: HireSense AI is not an autonomous hiring system. Predictions, match scores and recommendations should not be used as the sole basis for employment decisions. The 320-record dataset is balanced with 160 shortlisted and 160 not shortlisted candidates across five technical roles, but it is small and structurally similar, so prototype evaluation does not represent production hiring accuracy. Real deployment would require diverse lawfully collected anonymized data, bias and fairness evaluation, explainability, auditability and human review.

title: HireSense AI current improvement roadmap
content: Completed improvements are LLM timeout and retry handling, explicit unknown-category handling, and removal of the duplicate candidate-preview section. In progress are regression leakage correction, match-score retraining and re-evaluation, expanded automated tests, deployment preparation, dependency reproducibility and production security improvements, evaluation with more diverse data, and appropriate bias, fairness and auditability checks.

title: Kaushik’s Footprints overview
content: Kaushik’s Footprints is a full-stack fashion and lifestyle e-commerce application. It connects a React customer storefront and separate React admin interface through a Node.js and Express REST API with persistent MongoDB data. The verified current scope includes storefront browsing, categories, product details, JWT-based authentication, user-specific cart operations, product-image upload and catalogue management. It does not claim completed live payments or complete order persistence.

title: Kaushik’s Footprints implemented features
content: Kaushik’s Footprints supports product discovery, men/women/kids category browsing, product-detail pages with image/category/pricing information, signup and login, JWT-based authenticated requests, user-specific cart data persisted in MongoDB, cart quantity and amount calculation, and a separate admin interface to add, list and remove products and upload product images. Checkout is the next stage of the user journey; live payments are not presented as implemented.

title: Kaushik’s Footprints architecture and technologies
content: Kaushik’s Footprints uses React for customer and admin interfaces, Node.js and Express for REST API endpoints, MongoDB for products/users/user-specific cart data, JWT for token-based authenticated requests, and Multer for product-image uploads. The storefront and admin panel use the same Express API and MongoDB product collection. The customer frontend requests product, authentication and cart data; the admin panel uploads images and manages catalogue products, which become available in the storefront through the backend API.

title: Kaushik’s Footprints development challenges
content: Key Kaushik’s Footprints challenges included keeping storefront, admin and backend API contracts consistent; managing CORS across local development ports; persisting an independent authenticated cart for each user; attaching and verifying JWTs for protected cart operations; handling multipart image uploads and accessible image paths; synchronising admin catalogue changes with storefront product APIs; and separating customer/admin modules. Production preparation is next-stage engineering and would require environment configuration, secrets, password hashing, restricted admin endpoints, upload validation, production CORS and complete checkout handling.

title: Kaushik’s Footprints lessons learned
content: Kaushik’s Footprints reinforced that full-stack features require coordinated frontend state, API behaviour, database models and error handling; persistent cart state requires authentication and synchronisation; JWTs must be attached and verified consistently; images need multipart upload, storage and delivery workflows; shared APIs benefit separate customer/admin interfaces; and modular routes, components, services and models improve maintainability. Production readiness also requires validation, testing, monitoring, secret management and reliable deployment configuration.

title: Kaushik’s Footprints future improvements
content: Future improvements—not current features—include complete order persistence, a production-ready payment gateway, admin order management, search/sorting/filtering, inventory tracking, wishlist and order history, verified promo codes, image validation, environment-based configuration, password hashing, role-based admin authorization, automated tests, and production deployment of the storefront, admin panel, backend and database.

title: Agri-Products overview
content: Agri-Products is a full-stack agricultural marketplace prototype. It connects agricultural land and product listings, time-bound bidding, user accounts, search, bid tracking and real-time buyer-seller communication. Its frontend deployment target is Netlify, its backend deployment target is Render, and data is stored in MongoDB Atlas. The public demo is temporarily unavailable because the backend deployment is currently offline. The live demo can be restored after the backend has been fixed and redeployed.

title: Agri-Products features and workflow
content: Agri-Products supports email/password registration, Google sign-in integration, bcrypt password hashing, one-hour JWT authentication, password-reset email flow, land and agricultural-product listings, multiple-image uploads, paginated product browsing, land and product bid records, land search by location and type, My Listings, My Bids, My Wins, user profiles, Socket.IO chat and persisted messages. A node-cron task processes expired ongoing land auctions every minute, identifies the highest valid bid, updates the land-auction result and generates a PDF winner certificate with PDFKit. Product-auction winner automation is not claimed as implemented.

title: Agri-Products architecture and technologies
content: Agri-Products uses React 19, React Router, Context API, Axios and Socket.IO Client in the frontend. Its backend uses Node.js, Express, MongoDB with Mongoose, Socket.IO, JSON Web Tokens, bcrypt, Multer, Nodemailer, node-cron, PDFKit, CORS and dotenv. The application is a modular client-server architecture, not microservices. The backend separates routes, controllers, models, middleware and utilities. Socket.IO authenticates socket connections with the user token and chat messages are stored in MongoDB before being emitted to the recipient's socket room.

title: Agri-Products engineering status and challenges
content: Agri-Products is a full-stack prototype undergoing production hardening. Its public demo is temporarily unavailable because the backend deployment is currently offline. The production roadmap includes resolving merge-conflict markers, centralising API URLs in environment configuration, enforcing token-blacklist checks in authentication middleware, server-side Google credential verification, protected chat-history endpoints, consistent server-side bid validation, atomic conditional bid updates or transactions, expanded secured admin APIs, upload validation, durable cloud storage, rate limiting, structured validation, automated tests, monitoring and retry-safe scheduled processing. Concurrent bidding needs atomic updates or optimistic concurrency control so stale or simultaneous bids cannot overwrite one another.

title: Agri-Products future enhancements
content: Future improvements for Agri-Products, not current features, include payment integration with Razorpay or Stripe, auction and market analytics, price forecasting, personalised recommendations, regional-language support, map-based discovery, seller KYC, ratings and reviews, mobile applications, push notifications, expanded admin management, cloud object storage and transaction-safe concurrent bidding.
